description: Blackcurrant, black cherry and plum with cedar, graphite, tobacco leaf and a green bell pepper edge. Firm, drying tannin and fresh acidity.
notes: Usually blended with Merlot and Cabernet Franc. Graves and Haut-Médoc gravel soils lend a pencil-shaving minerality; new French oak is subtle compared to Napa.
confusion: Merlot (Right Bank) is rounder with softer tannin; Cabernet Franc shows more red fruit and pyrazine; New World Cabernet is riper with more oak and alcohol.

region: Napa Valley & Sonoma, California; Australia; Chile
description: Ripe cassis, blackberry and black cherry, mint or eucalyptus, cocoa and lavish vanilla and toast from new oak. Full body with high, ripe tannin.
notes: Napa shows the plushest fruit and most oak. Coonawarra and Margaret River (Australia) show mint/eucalyptus; Chile's Central Valley often keeps a pyrazine note.
confusion: New World Merlot is softer and less tannic; Australian Shiraz shows more blue fruit and lower acidity; Zinfandel is jammier with higher alcohol.

description: Plum, black cherry and red currant with tobacco, cocoa, earth and a light herbal note. Rounder and fleshier than Left Bank Cabernet.
notes: Blended with Cabernet Franc. Clay soils in Pomerol give density and truffle-like earth.
confusion: Left Bank Cabernet is more tannic and structured; Cabernet Franc is leaner with more pyrazine.

description: Ripe plum, black cherry and blackberry with mocha, chocolate and vanilla. Plush, round tannin and moderate acidity.
notes: Often the softest, most approachable of the Bordeaux varieties in California.
confusion: New World Cabernet has firmer tannin and more structure; Zinfandel is jammier with spice and higher alcohol.

description: Tart cherry, raspberry and cranberry with forest floor, mushroom, dried leaves and wet stone. Light to medium body, silky tannin, bright acidity.
notes: Village and Premier Cru wines see a moderate amount of French oak. Earth often rivals fruit.
confusion: Gamay (Cru Beaujolais) is fruitier with carbonic notes; Nebbiolo has far more tannin and acidity; Oregon Pinot can be very similar.

region: California; Willamette Valley, Oregon; New Zealand
description: Ripe black and red cherry, raspberry, cola and baking spice with vanilla. More fruit-forward than Burgundy with softer acidity.
notes: California is the ripest; Oregon and Central Otago sit between California and Burgundy; Martinborough leans savory.
confusion: Burgundy shows more earth and acidity; Grenache is riper, higher in alcohol and less acidic.

description: Bright raspberry, strawberry, cherry and cranberry with violet and peony, plus banana, bubblegum or kirsch from carbonic maceration. Low tannin, fresh acidity.
notes: Cru Beaujolais (Morgon, Moulin-à-Vent) from granite soils is more structured and earthy, with less obvious carbonic character.
confusion: Burgundy Pinot Noir is earthier with more oak and finer tannin; young Grenache is higher in alcohol.

description: Ripe to jammy strawberry, raspberry and kirsch with garrigue (dried thyme, lavender, rosemary), white pepper, leather and earth. Warm alcohol, modest acidity.
notes: Blended with Syrah and Mourvèdre (GSM). Aged in large old foudres, so little new oak. Garnet rim even when young.
confusion: Australian Grenache is fruitier with less earth; Zinfandel is darker with more oak; Tempranillo shows more oak and leather.

description: Jammy raspberry, strawberry and red plum with sweet spice and a light herbal note. Fleshy, high in alcohol, soft acidity.
notes: Old bush vines in the Barossa and McLaren Vale; often blended with Shiraz and Mataro (Mourvèdre).
confusion: Southern Rhône Grenache is earthier and more savory; Zinfandel is darker with more oak and spice.

description: Blackberry, black plum and blueberry with violet, cracked black pepper, smoked meat, bacon fat, olive and iron.
notes: Côte-Rôtie may be co-fermented with a little Viognier for perfume. Granite soils add a stony, mineral note.
confusion: Australian Shiraz is riper with more oak and less pepper and meat; Left Bank Bordeaux shows pyrazine and cedar.

region: South Australia, Western Australia & Victoria; California
description: Jammy blackberry, blueberry and black plum with licorice, dark chocolate, eucalyptus or mint and sweet American or French oak.
notes: Barossa is the ripest and most opulent; Victoria and Western Australia are cooler and more peppery. California Syrah sits between Australia and the Rhône.
confusion: Zinfandel is jammier with more red fruit; New World Cabernet has firmer tannin and less blue fruit; Malbec is less spicy.

description: Deep purple with blackberry, black plum and blueberry, violet, cocoa and sweet vanilla oak. Plush and full-bodied with soft-to-moderate tannin.
notes: High-altitude vineyards give intense color and keep acidity fresher than the warm days suggest.
confusion: Australian Shiraz has more spice and mint; New World Merlot is less purple and less floral.

description: Pale garnet with an orange rim. Sour and dried cherry, rose, tar, licorice, dried herbs and earth. Very high tannin and acidity.
notes: The color is deceptively light for the power on the palate. Traditional producers age in large neutral botti.
confusion: Sangiovese is less tannic with tomato leaf and oregano; Pinot Noir is far softer; aged Grenache is lower in acid.

region: Chianti Classico & Brunello di Montalcino, Tuscany, Italy
description: Sour cherry, red plum and dried cranberry with tomato leaf, oregano, black tea, balsamic, leather and dusty earth. High acid and drying tannin.
notes: Brunello is fuller and more powerful than Chianti Classico. Riserva sees longer oak aging.
confusion: Nebbiolo is paler with more tannin, tar and rose; Tempranillo has more obvious oak and dill.

description: Dried cherry, strawberry and plum with tobacco, leather, dill, coconut and vanilla from American oak. Reserva and Gran Reserva show oxidative, savory character.
notes: Rioja traditionally uses American oak; Ribera del Duero is darker and more powerful, often with French oak.
confusion: Sangiovese has higher acid and less oak; Southern Rhône Grenache has more alcohol and garrigue.

region: Napa Valley, Paso Robles & Sonoma, California
description: Jammy blackberry, raspberry and plum with raisin and prune, sweet baking spice, black pepper and American oak. Very high alcohol.
notes: Uneven ripening means fresh, jammy and raisined berries in the same bunch. Old-vine Sonoma examples are more structured.
confusion: Australian Shiraz has more blue fruit and mint; Australian Grenache is lighter in color with more red fruit.
